title: Danny Boyle on Ink and Slumdog Millionaire's Near Miss
excerpt:
The Oscar-winning filmmaker discussed media history and career turning points.
He recalled how Slumdog Millionaire narrowly avoided a direct-to-video release.
body_md:
Speaking at the SCAD Savannah Film Festival, where he received the Maverick Director Award, Danny Boyle discussed his new film Ink alongside several defining experiences from his career. Ink explores the 1969 encounter between Rupert Murdoch and newspaperman Larry Lamb and the evolution of tabloid journalism.

Boyle sees connections between that historical shift and the modern media environment. Rather than reducing Murdoch to a conventional villain, he wanted to acknowledge his reservations while examining the consequences of his failure to act on them.

Netflix has scheduled the film for a theatrical release on December 11, 2026, followed by streaming on January 8, 2027.

Boyle also revisited the famous toilet sequence in Trainspotting. The production relied on practical scenery and optical illusion rather than early computer-generated effects. Ewan McGregor's movements helped sell the illusion, while the unpleasant-looking material was actually chocolate.

Another striking recollection concerned Slumdog Millionaire. A management change at Warner Bros. threatened to send several films directly to video, including Boyle's project. Peter Rice at Fox Searchlight acquired it, believing its appeal would become clear when screened for audiences.

The film ultimately brought Boyle Academy Award, Golden Globe and BAFTA directing honors. Its journey illustrates how distribution decisions can dramatically alter a film's prospects.
